comparisons.peer_summary: Citi held $35.9 billion of purchased credit protection, including $33.7 billion in credit derivatives on individual entities and $2.2 billion in first loss tranches of portfolio derivatives.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and Citi disclose the use of purchased credit protection to hedge funded and unfunded credit exposures, providing specific notional amounts. BAC reported net notional purchased protection of $10.4 billion, while Citi held a larger total of $35.9 billion, broken down into $33.7 billion in individual entity credit derivatives and $2.2 billion in first loss tranches of portfolio derivatives. Both disclosures explicitly categorize these instruments as derivatives used for economic hedging of credit risk.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net CDS Hedges Composition and Basis
comparisons.peer_summary: The disclosed amounts include net CDS hedges on counterparty exposure and lending, executed by trading desks, based on CDS notional amounts assuming zero recovery adjusted for fair value of receivables/payables.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose the use of net credit default swaps (CDS) to hedge credit risk. BAC purchases credit protection to cover funded and unfunded exposures and sells protection to manage costs, resulting in $10.4 billion in net notional purchased protection. MS reports net CDS hedges (purchased and sold) on counterparty exposure and lending, calculated based on notional amounts assuming zero recovery. Both firms actively manage their credit derivative books by buying and selling protection.

sentences.text: We purchase credit protection to cover the funded portion as well as the unfunded portion of certain credit exposures.
To lower the cost of obtaining our desired credit protection levels, we may add credit exposure within an industry, borrower or counterparty group by selling protection.

At December 31, 2024 and 2023, net notional credit default protection purchased in our credit derivatives portfolio to hedge our funded and unfunded exposures for which we elected the fair value option, as well as certain other credit exposures, was $10.4 billion and $10.9 billion.
Amounts represent net CDS hedges (purchased and sold) on net counterparty exposure and lending executed by trading desks responsible for hedging counterparty and lending credit risk exposures.
Amounts are based on the CDS notional amount assuming zero recovery adjusted for the fair value of any receivable or payable.
